message.reasoning_content:
Record the top 3 claims: layout cross-consistency (probe with N not multiple of 64? N=65 in make_inputs — interesting, N=65 not multiple of 64 covers partial tile); group indexing by kk//GROUP_SIZE (partial final group with K not multiple of group_size — e.g. K=17, group_size=16: group 1 has 1 row; sorted kk=16 -> group 1, fine. Actually check G=ceil(K/group_size) — if K=17, gs=16, G=2, groups sizes 16,1 — sorted index kk//16 gives group 0 for kk<16, group 1 for kk=16. OK. But if K=128, gs=48? Not allowed. Fine.) Actually the histogram check: group g occurs min(gs, K-g*gs) — with G=ceil(K/gs), last group size = K-(G-1)gs which matches min. OK.

Third: H16 rounding with scale conversion — kernel loads scale .to(tl.float32) from FP16; product (quant-zero)*scale in FP32 exact? 4-bit int times fp16 value: exact in fp32 yes. Then .to(fp16) round-to-nearest-even? Triton fp32->fp16 cast rounding mode assumed RTNE. Tie cases: scale = power of 2 with odd int difference creates exact halfway in fp16? e.g. (q-z)=±1, scale=2^-24 subnormal fp16 → product subnormal fp16. scale must be in (0,1/32], fp16 min subnormal 2^-24 ~6e-8 allowed. Halfway ties: need fp16 exactly representable product? For ties, need product exactly halfway between fp16 values. E.g. (q-z)=3, scale=1/3? fp16 scale ~0.33325... Actually exact halfway requires product = midpoint of two fp16 numbers. With scale power of two, product is exact in fp16 — no tie. Ties: scale = (midpoint)/(q-z). fp16 scale values limited. Possible. This is a legit claim to probe.

Record 3 claims: (1) layout inversion mismatch (in_scope, risk of silently permuted weights — testable by comparing to reference); (2) group indexing / partial group or ordering issue — actually more useful: probe run vs reference across shapes K not multiple of 16 and group_size mismatches; (3) fp16 rounding of decoded weight (ties/subnormal). Scope: contract explicitly defines D=H16(...), so in-scope.
